```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alabdulkarim_2026_amikacin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alabdulkarim_2026_amikacin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkag354> (open access, PMC13688210)

The model was first developed in 204 neonates, evaluated without re-estimation
in 205 older children, and then refitted to all 409 patients. This file holds
the refitted, final model ("Final model" column of Table S5, Table 2). The
authors published their nlmixr2 code for that model (Supplementary Code S1);
its estimates agree with Table 2 to the printed precision, so the full-precision
values from the code are used.

# Population

Retrospective therapeutic drug monitoring data from 409 patients at Great
Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London (September 2020 to December 2022)
who received intravenous amikacin for at least 3 days (Methods; Table 1):
204 neonates (birth to < 1 month), 72 aged 1 month to 2 years, 41 aged 3-6
years, 52 aged 7-12 years and 40 aged 13-18 years. Median age 0.12 years
(range 0.003-18), weight 4.73 kg (0.6-143), postmenstrual age 44 weeks
(24-992), serum creatinine 41 umol/L (7-770); 55.7% male; 14.2% received a
concomitant glycopeptide. Doses were 5-30 mg/kg (median 15 mg/kg), almost all
once daily; doses of 20 mg/kg or more were given as 30-min infusions and lower
doses as about 3-min slow bolus injections. There were 1091 concentrations
(median 2 per patient), 26.6% below the 0.8 mg/L quantification limit.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Alabdulkarim_2026_amikacin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, 70 kg) | log scale 1.7285 (5.633 L/h) | Code S1 `tcl`; Table 2 'CL (L/h/70 kg)' 5.634 |
| `lvc` (V1, 70 kg) | log scale 3.3789 (29.34 L) | Code S1 `tv`; Table 2 'V1' 29.34 |
| `lq` (Q, 70 kg) | log scale 0.0631 (1.065 L/h) | Code S1 `tq`; Table 2 'Q' 1.07 |
| `lvp` (V2, 70 kg) | log scale 3.4098 (30.26 L) | Code S1 `tvp`; Table 2 'V2' 30.26 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods Eq. 1; Code S1 `beta.wt.cl` (applied to CL and Q) |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Methods Eq. 1; Code S1 `beta.wt.v` (applied to V1 and V2) |
| `tmat50` | 47.7 weeks (fixed) | Methods 'Covariate model', Eq. 2 |
| `hill_mat` | 3.4 (fixed) | Methods 'Covariate model', Eq. 2 |
| `e_creat_cl` | -0.72449 | Code S1 `beta.cr.cl`; Table 2 'beta Scr (CL)' -0.73 |
| `cl_pna_famp` | -0.55913 (= hM - 1) | Code S1 `hM` = 0.44087; Table 2 'hM (CL)' 0.44 |
| `lcl_pna_kdes` | log(0.28392) 1/day | Code S1 `hN`; Table 2 'hN (CL)' 0.28 |
| `e_conmed_glycopeptide_cl` | -0.20576 | Code S1 `beta.glycopeptide`; Table 2 -0.21 |
| IIV block on CL, V1, Q, V2 | 4x4 variance-covariance | Code S1 `eta.cl + eta.v + eta.q + eta.vp ~ c(...)`; diagonal CVs match Table S5 'Final model' (49.93, 22.80, 91.40, 32.70%) |
| `propSd` | 0.2489 | Code S1 `prop.err`; Table 2 24.89% |
| `addSd` | 1.020 mg/L | Code S1 `add.err`; Table 2 1.020 mg/L |
| Allometry `(WT/70)^beta` | n/a | Methods Eq. 1; Table 2 equations |
| PMA maturation `PMA^3.4 / (47.7^3.4 + PMA^3.4)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 2 |
| Typical creatinine `-2.37330 - 12.91367 ln(PNA_y) + 23.93581 PNA_y^0.5` | n/a | Methods Eq. 3 (Ceriotti 2008) |
| Creatinine factor `(Scr / TSCR)^beta_Scr` | n/a | Methods Eq. 4 |
| Postnatal factor `hM + (1 - hM)(1 - exp(-PNA_d hN))` | n/a | Methods Eq. 5; Code S1 `maturation_pna` |
| Glycopeptide factor `exp(beta * glycopeptide)` | n/a | Code S1 `cl` expression |
| Two-compartment ODEs | n/a | Code S1 `d/dt(A1)`, `d/dt(A2)` |
| Combined residual error | n/a | Code S1 `cp ~ prop(prop.err) + add(add.err)` |

A check that the IIV block reproduces the published coefficients of
variation, computed as `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`. The code's block matches the
"Final model" column of Table S5 exactly; Table 2 prints 91.50% rather than
91.40% for Q (and differs by 0.01 points for CL and V1).

```{r iiv-check}
mod <- readModelDb("Alabdulkarim_2026_amikacin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
cv_pct <- 100 * sqrt(exp(diag(ui$omega)) - 1)
cv_s5 <- c(etalcl = 49.93, etalvc = 22.80, etalq = 91.40, etalvp = 32.70)
cv_t2 <- c(etalcl = 49.94, etalvc = 22.79, etalq = 91.50, etalvp = 32.70)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    eta = names(cv_s5), model = round(cv_pct[names(cv_s5)], 2),
    Table_S5 = cv_s5, Table_2 = cv_t2
  ),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "IIV as CV% from the packaged omega block vs. Tables S5 and 2."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(cv_pct[names(cv_s5)] - cv_s5) < 0.006))
```

# Typical patients across the age range

Typical-value profiles (no random effects, no glycopeptide) for a patient with
the Table 1 median covariates of each age group, receiving 15 mg/kg once daily
as a 3-min injection for 72 h, the regimen and horizon of the paper's
simulations. Postnatal age is supplied in months and postmenstrual age in
weeks.

```{r typical}
typical <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~age_y, ~PAGE, ~WT, ~CREAT,
  "Neonate", 0.01, 39, 2.87, 48,
  "1 month-2 years", 0.29, 54, 7.7, 24.5,
  "3-6 years", 4.1, 258, 16.7, 32,
  "7-12 years", 10, 565, 33.6, 42.5,
  "13-18 years", 15, 829, 48.5, 56
) |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    PNA = age_y * 12,
    CONMED_GLYCOPEPTIDE = 0L,
    group = factor(group, levels = group)
  )

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  typical |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 24, 48)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 15 * WT, rate = amt / 0.05),
  typical |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Amikacin concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical patient by age group, 15 mg/kg q24h",
    caption = "Dashed line: 5 mg/L trough safety target."
  )
```

The typical clearance per kilogram rises steeply over the neonatal period and
then falls with size, as expected for allometric scaling with renal maturation:

```{r typical-cl}
sim_typ |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  distinct(group, cl, vc) |>
  left_join(typical |> select(group, WT), by = "group") |>
  mutate(cl_per_kg = cl / WT, vc_per_kg = vc / WT) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age group" = group, "Weight (kg)" = WT, "CL (L/h)" = cl, "V1 (L)" = vc,
    "CL (L/h/kg)" = cl_per_kg, "V1 (L/kg)" = vc_per_kg
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical parameters at the Table 1 median covariates.")
```

# Virtual cohort

The authors simulated 500 patients per age group by resampling their own
patients, whose covariates are not public. The virtual cohort below
approximates Table 1 group by group (200 per arm):

* Neonates are split as in Figure 4 into postnatal age 1-7 days and 8-28 days.
  Gestational age is term (37-42 weeks) for 70% and preterm (24-37 weeks)
  for 30%, which reproduces the 39-week median postmenstrual age; weight
  follows a median birth-weight-for-postmenstrual-age curve with 12% CV.
* Older children have age log-uniform within the group's Table 1 range,
  postmenstrual age = 40 weeks + postnatal age, and weight from a median
  weight-for-age curve with 15% CV.
* Serum creatinine is the Ceriotti age-expected value scaled so that the group
  median matches Table 1, with 35% log-normal scatter.
* Glycopeptide use follows the Table 1 percentage of each group.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
n_per_arm <- 200

ceriotti_tscr <- function(age_y) -2.37330 - 12.91367 * log(age_y) + 23.93581 * sqrt(age_y)

wt_for_age <- data.frame(
  age = c(0.08, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18),
  wt = c(4.5, 6, 7.8, 9.6, 12.2, 14.3, 16.3, 18.3, 20.5, 25.6, 32, 40, 50, 58, 64)
)
wt_for_pma <- data.frame(pma = c(24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44), wt = c(0.65, 1.1, 1.7, 2.6, 3.5, 4.6))

groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~creat_med, ~age_med, ~p_glyco,
  "Neonate, PNA <= 7 d", 1 / 365.25, 7 / 365.25, 48, 0.01, 0.118,
  "Neonate, PNA > 7 d", 8 / 365.25, 28 / 365.25, 48, 0.01, 0.118,
  "1 month-2 years", 0.08, 2.33, 24.5, 0.29, 0.181,
  "3-6 years", 3.03, 6.27, 32, 4.1, 0.146,
  "7-12 years", 7, 12.28, 42.5, 10, 0.135,
  "13-18 years", 13, 18, 56, 15, 0.20
)

make_group <- function(g, n) {
  neonate <- startsWith(g$group, "Neonate")
  if (neonate) {
    age_y <- runif(n, g$age_lo, g$age_hi)
    ga <- ifelse(runif(n) < 0.7, runif(n, 37, 42), runif(n, 24, 37))
    pma <- ga + age_y * 365.25 / 7
    wt <- approx(wt_for_pma$pma, wt_for_pma$wt, pma, rule = 2)$y * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.12))
  } else {
    age_y <- exp(runif(n, log(g$age_lo), log(g$age_hi)))
    pma <- 40 + age_y * 365.25 / 7
    wt <- approx(wt_for_age$age, wt_for_age$wt, age_y, rule = 2)$y * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.15))
  }
  creat_ratio <- g$creat_med / ceriotti_tscr(g$age_med)
  tibble(
    group = g$group,
    PNA = age_y * 12,
    PAGE = pma,
    WT = wt,
    CREAT = ceriotti_tscr(age_y) * creat_ratio * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.35)),
    CONMED_GLYCOPEPTIDE = as.integer(runif(n) < g$p_glyco)
  )
}

cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups)), function(i) make_group(groups[i, ], n_per_arm)))

cohort |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = groups$group)) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    `Weight (kg)` = median(WT), `PMA (weeks)` = median(PAGE),
    `Scr (umol/L)` = median(CREAT), `Glycopeptide (%)` = 100 * mean(CONMED_GLYCOPEPTIDE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort medians by age group.")
```

# Probability of target attainment (Table S7, Figures 3-6)

The paper's targets are Cmax/MIC >= 10 for efficacy and a trough below 5 mg/L
for safety, both evaluated over the last dosing interval ending at 72 h
(Methods 'Simulation and probability of target attainment'). For a
two-compartment model with intravenous dosing the maximum of that interval is
at the end of the last infusion and the minimum is at 72 h, so two
observations per patient suffice. Doses of 20 mg/kg or more are 30-min
infusions and smaller doses 3-min injections (Methods 'Amikacin dosing and
sampling'). The PK is linear, so one solve per patient and administration mode
covers every dose: 10 mg/kg (3-min) is scaled to 5 and 15 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg
(30-min) to 25, 30 and 35 mg/kg. Concentrations are individual predictions
without residual error.

```{r pta-sim}
regimens <- tidyr::expand_grid(group = groups$group, tau = c(24, 12, 8), ref_mgkg = c(10, 20))

make_regimen_events <- function(r, cohort, id_offset) {
  cg <- cohort[cohort$group == r$group, ]
  cg$id <- id_offset + seq_len(nrow(cg))
  dur <- if (r$ref_mgkg >= 20) 0.5 else 0.05
  t_last <- 72 - r$tau
  doses <- cg |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, t_last, by = r$tau)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = r$ref_mgkg * WT, rate = amt / dur)
  obs <- cg |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = c(t_last + dur, 72)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", tau = r$tau, ref_mgkg = r$ref_mgkg)
}

ev_pta <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(k) {
  make_regimen_events(regimens[k, ], cohort, id_offset = (k - 1L) * n_per_arm)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_pta[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, ev_pta,
  keep = c("group", "tau", "ref_mgkg"), returnType = "data.frame"
)

exposure_ref <- sim_pta |>
  group_by(id, group, tau, ref_mgkg) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), cmin = Cc[which.max(time)], .groups = "drop")

dose_map <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ref_mgkg, ~mgkg,
  10, 5, 10, 10, 10, 15,
  20, 20, 20, 25, 20, 30, 20, 35
)
exposure <- exposure_ref |>
  inner_join(dose_map, by = "ref_mgkg", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(cmax = cmax * mgkg / ref_mgkg, cmin = cmin * mgkg / ref_mgkg)
```

```{r table-s7}
  mutate(diff = simulated - published)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_s7) == 3 * nrow(published_s7))

  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", simulated, published)) |>
  select(group, tau, mgkg, endpoint, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = endpoint, values_from = cell) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age group" = group, "Interval (h)" = tau, "Dose (mg/kg)" = mgkg,
    "Efficacy PTA, MIC 2 (sim / pub %)" = eff_mic2,
    "Efficacy PTA, MIC 4 (sim / pub %)" = eff_mic4,

```

```{r table-s7-summary}
cmp_s7 |>
  group_by(endpoint) |>
  summarise(
    median_abs_diff = median(abs(diff)),
    p90_abs_diff = unname(quantile(abs(diff), 0.9)),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Absolute differences, simulated minus published, in percentage points.")

# A mis-transcribed clearance, volume or covariate exponent moves whole
# columns of Table S7 by tens of percentage points; the virtual cohort only
# approximates the authors' resampled patients and each cell carries about
# 3.5 points of Monte Carlo error at 200 patients, so the gate is on the
# centre and on a robust upper quantile of the 162 cell differences.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(cmp_s7$diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(cmp_s7$diff), 0.9) < 15
)
```

## Figures 4-6: PTA across MIC by regimen

```{r figures-4-6, fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
mic_grid <- 2^seq(-3, 4)
pta_curves <- exposure |>
  filter(mgkg %in% c(10, 15, 20)) |>
  tidyr::crossing(mic = mic_grid) |>
  group_by(group, tau, mgkg, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(cmax / mic >= 10), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = groups$group),
    interval = factor(paste0("q", tau, "h"), levels = c("q24h", "q12h", "q8h"))
  )

ggplot(pta_curves, aes(mic, pta, colour = interval)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mic_grid, labels = format(mic_grid)) +
  facet_grid(group ~ paste(mgkg, "mg/kg")) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Efficacy PTA, Cmax/MIC >= 10 (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the efficacy panels of Figures 4-6 of Alabdulkarim 2026."
  )
```

```{r figures-4-6-safety}
exposure |>
  filter(mgkg %in% c(10, 15, 20)) |>
  group_by(group, tau, mgkg) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(cmin < 5), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = groups$group),
    interval = factor(paste0("q", tau, "h"), levels = c("q24h", "q12h", "q8h"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(mgkg), pta, fill = interval)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (mg/kg)", y = "Safety PTA, trough < 5 mg/L (%)", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the safety panels of Figures 4-6 of Alabdulkarim 2026."
  )
```

## Figure 3: once-daily dose comparison

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
sim1 <- exposure |>
  filter(tau == 24) |>
  tidyr::crossing(mic = mic_grid) |>
  group_by(group, mgkg, mic) |>
  summarise(efficacy = 100 * mean(cmax / mic >= 10), safety = 100 * mean(cmin < 5), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = groups$group))

ggplot(sim1, aes(mic, efficacy, colour = factor(mgkg))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mic_grid, labels = format(mic_grid)) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Efficacy PTA (%)", colour = "Dose (mg/kg)",
    caption = "Replicates the efficacy panels of Figure 3 (SIM1, q24h) of Alabdulkarim 2026."
  )

sim1 |>
  distinct(group, mgkg, safety) |>
  arrange(group, mgkg) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mgkg, values_from = safety, names_prefix = "mg/kg ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Age group" = group) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Safety PTA (%) for once-daily dosing, Figure 3 (SIM1).")
```

The paper's text states that 15-20 mg/kg once daily achieved more than 95% PTA
at an MIC of 2 mg/L in every age group (Results 'Probability of target
attainment'):

```{r claim-15-20}
claim <- simulated_s7 |> filter(tau == 24, mgkg %in% c(15, 20))
knitr::kable(claim, digits = 1, caption = "Once-daily 15-20 mg/kg, efficacy PTA at MIC 2 mg/L.")
stopifnot(all(claim$eff_mic2 > 90))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental results. As a self-consistency check,
the virtual cohort (100 patients per age group, with between-subject
variability) receives 15 mg/kg once daily as 3-min injections for 72 h with a
rich sampling grid, and PKNCA computes the first-dose and last-interval
exposure.

```{r pknca-sim}
nca_cohort <- cohort |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice_head(n = 100) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  nca_cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 24, 48)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 15 * WT, rate = amt / 0.05),
  nca_cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 1), 48 + c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5))))) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev_nca |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, group),
  amt ~ time | group + id
)
# Cmin only over the last interval: over the first dose it is the pre-dose zero.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 48), end = c(24, 72),
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE), auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(group, start, end, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = groups$group)) |>
  arrange(group, start)

nca_tab |>
  mutate(interval = paste0(start, "-", end, " h")) |>
  select(group, interval, cmax, cmin, auclast) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age group" = group, "Interval" = interval, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin, "AUC (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median PKNCA results, 15 mg/kg q24h (Cmin over the last interval only).")

# A 15 mg/kg dose into a central volume of about 0.42 L/kg gives a peak near
# 36 mg/L in every age group; a units or volume error would move it several-fold.
peak_last <- nca_tab |> filter(start == 48)
stopifnot(all(peak_last$cmax > 20), all(peak_last$cmax < 60))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final model only.** The paper reports two parameter sets: the model
  developed in neonates (evaluated externally in older children) and the same
  model refitted to all 409 patients. Only the refitted model, which the
  authors present as their final, unified model, is packaged.
- **Values from the authors' code.** All estimates are taken at full precision
  from Supplementary Code S1, which the authors describe as the code of the
  final model fitted to the combined dataset. They match Table 2 except for a
  rounding difference: the creatinine exponent is -0.72449 in the code and is
  printed as -0.73 in Tables 2 and S5.
  The between-subject CVs implied by the code's omega block match Table S5
  (49.93, 22.80, 91.40 and 32.70%); Table 2 prints 91.50% for Q, 0.1 points
  higher, and 0.01-point differences for CL and V1.
- **Glycopeptide effect.** The Table 2 and Table S2 equations write the effect
  as `(glycopeptides)^beta`, which cannot be evaluated for a 0/1 indicator. The
  code uses `exp(beta * glycopeptide)` inside the clearance exponent, which is
  what was fitted and is used here (clearance 18.6% lower with a glycopeptide).
  The paper does not list the glycopeptides involved.
- **Postnatal maturation reparameterised.** Eq. 5,
  `hM + (1 - hM)(1 - exp(-PNA hN))`, is algebraically identical to
  `1 + (hM - 1) exp(-hN PNA)`; it is stored as `cl_pna_famp = hM - 1` and
  `lcl_pna_kdes = log(hN)` so that it uses the library's established names for
  a birth effect that decays over postnatal age. Predictions are unchanged.
- **Typical creatinine computed inside the model.** The Ceriotti polynomial
  (Eq. 3) is evaluated from postnatal age in years, recovered from the
  canonical postnatal age in months; postnatal age in days for Eq. 5 uses
  30.4375 days per month. The polynomial contains `ln(age)`, so postnatal age
  must be greater than zero. The paper does not state whether the polynomial
  was capped at older ages; it is applied as printed up to 18 years.
- **Postmenstrual age in weeks.** The model takes `PAGE` in weeks, the unit of
  the Rhodin constants, rather than the library's default of months.
- **Virtual cohort.** The authors resampled their own patients for the
  simulations; the cohort here is synthetic and matched to the Table 1 medians
  as described above. The neonatal postnatal-age strata (1-7 and 8-28 days),
  the 70/30 term/preterm split and the growth curves are the maintainers'
  assumptions. The Table S7 differences reflect these approximations and Monte
  Carlo error (about 3.5 percentage points per cell).
- **PTA details not stated in the paper.** Whether the authors' simulated
  concentrations included residual error is not stated; individual predictions
  without residual error are used. The 3-min injection is simulated as a
  0.05-h infusion.
- **Below-quantification data.** The M3 method used in estimation has no
  counterpart in simulation.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as
  of 2026-11-18.
